pr_title: SQL: Fix MIN, MAX, SUM aggs data type handling
pr_body:
This fixes the way the MIN, MAX and SUM aggs handle the returned data types:
- MIN and MAX must return the same data type as input's.
- SUM must return long/BIGINT for integral types and double otherwise.

The fix concerns both data returned in projections, as well as aggs script
filtering.

Fixes #71390, #65413.
pr_comments:
> We likely need a dedicated script method that relies on `Number`.longValue() and such plus null casting.

I wanted to also propose an inline alternative before as well (as updated), but if a wrapping function is preferable, I'll update to that.
> 
> I'd like to see this case in our tests to make sure it works properly (such as MIN, MAX and SUM over a fields that are null):
> 
> `SELECT MAX(field) WHERE fields IS NULL`

These have been added.

issue_context.title: QL: handing integer inexact division
issue_context.body:
Stumbled into that and took a while to figure it out.
Regardless of the type of a division, we do not perform rounding which leads to obscure results.
Take `x / 100 > 745`
For `x = 74572` this results in
```
74572 / 100 > 745 == 745.72 > 745      // true <-- incorrect
74572 / 100 = (int) 745.72 = 745 > 745 // false
```

Considering we should preserve the type, at least in SQL we need to enforce this inside our `ArithemticOperations`.`SimplifyComparisonsArithmetics` for example takes this into account.
